## 1. Purpose

This SOP describes the use of the standard Secchi disk and the Secchi
disk tube (transparency tube) for measuring water transparency in
lakes, reservoirs, and streams. Secchi depth is one of the oldest and
simplest limnological measurements, providing a rapid estimate of the
photic zone depth and an index of suspended particle concentration. The
Secchi tube adapts the same principle for shallow or wadeable waters
where a standard disk cannot be deployed vertically.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Visual transparency measurements in lakes, ponds,
  reservoirs (standard Secchi disk) and streams, shallow wetlands, and
  stormwater basins (Secchi tube)
- **Does not apply to:** Quantitative turbidity measurements (see
  [SOP-F205](SOP-F205-handheld-turbidity-meter.qmd)); laboratory
  transmissometry; PAR light profiles (requires underwater quantum
  sensor)
- **Location:** All EA Program surface water field sites


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Specify measurement protocol for the project            |
| Trained Personnel | Perform measurements per this SOP                       |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use                |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Secchi disk measurements from boats, docks, or bridges
  require caution to prevent falls. Wear a personal flotation device
  (PFD) when sampling from boats.
- **Biological:** Surface water may contain pathogens. Avoid
  ingestion; wear gloves if hands contact water.
- **Sun glare:** Measuring Secchi depth requires looking directly into
  water; wear polarized sunglasses to reduce glare and improve
  accuracy (but note this in the field notebook for consistency).
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Closed-toed shoes or wading boots
- [ ] Personal flotation device (boat sampling)
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (optional; recommended for impaired waters)
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunglasses)

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd). If
sampling from a boat, ensure all occupants know the location of PFDs
and throwable flotation devices.


## 5. Equipment and Materials

### Standard Secchi Disk

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Standard Secchi disk (20 cm diameter) | Alternating black and white quadrants; weighted to sink horizontally |
| Graduated line (marked every 0.1 m)   | Non-stretch braided cord or chain        |
| Viewscope (optional)                  | Eliminates surface glare; a section of PVC pipe with a clear bottom works well |

### Secchi Tube (Transparency Tube)

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Secchi tube (60 or 120 cm)            | Clear acrylic tube with a Secchi disk pattern at the bottom and a cm/inch scale printed on the side; drain valve at the base |
| Sample bucket or wide-mouth bottle    | For collecting water to pour into the tube |

### General

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Field notebook                        | For recording measurements               |
| Stopwatch or watch                    | For recording time of measurement        |
| Camera                                | For photo-documenting site conditions    |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Standard Secchi Disk (Lakes, Reservoirs, Deep Pools)

Secchi disk measurements should be taken on the shaded side of the
boat or dock between 10:00 and 14:00 local time for consistency. Avoid
measurements during heavy cloud cover, rain, or high wind (waves
disturb the reading).

1. Lower the Secchi disk on the shaded side of the boat until it just
   disappears from view. Record this depth as **D1** (disappearance
   depth).
2. Slowly raise the disk until it just reappears. Record this depth as
   **D2** (reappearance depth).
3. Calculate Secchi depth:

   $$
   \text{Secchi depth} = \frac{D1 + D2}{2}
   $$

4. Record in the field notebook:
   - Secchi depth (m)
   - Date and time
   - Sky conditions (clear, partly cloudy, overcast)
   - Wind conditions (calm, light, moderate)
   - Whether a viewscope was used
   - Water surface conditions (calm, rippled, choppy)
   - Observer name (Secchi readings vary between observers)
5. If the disk is visible on the bottom, record "Secchi depth >
   [bottom depth]" and note the bottom depth.
6. Repeat the measurement a second time. The two readings should agree
   within 0.5 m. Record both and report the mean.

### 6.2 Secchi Tube (Streams, Shallow Waters)

Use the Secchi tube when the water body is too shallow for a standard
disk or when sampling from shore.

1. Collect a water sample from the site using a bucket or wide-mouth
   bottle. Sample from mid-depth if possible; avoid collecting from
   the surface film or disturbing sediment.
2. Pour the sample into the Secchi tube until the tube is full.
3. Hold the tube vertically and look down through the water column at
   the Secchi pattern on the bottom.
4. Open the drain valve slowly, allowing water to drain from the
   bottom. Watch the Secchi pattern.
5. When the Secchi pattern just disappears, close the valve and read
   the water level on the graduated scale. Record this as the
   **Secchi tube depth** (cm).
6. Refill the tube and repeat the measurement. The two readings should
   agree within 2 cm. Record both and report the mean.
7. Rinse the tube with DI water between sites to prevent cross-
   contamination.


## 7. Data Interpretation

Secchi depth is inversely related to turbidity and suspended particle
concentration. Approximate relationships (lake conditions):

| Secchi Depth (m) | General Water Clarity       |
|:-----------------|:----------------------------|
| > 5              | Very clear (oligotrophic)   |
| 2--5             | Moderately clear (mesotrophic) |
| 1--2             | Turbid (eutrophic)          |
| < 1              | Very turbid (hypereutrophic) |

::: {.callout-note}
These categories are approximate and vary with dissolved color, algal
species, and suspended sediment type. Do not use Secchi depth alone to
classify trophic state; combine with nutrient and chlorophyll data.
:::


## 8. Quality Control

- Use the same observer for repeated measurements at a monitoring site
  whenever possible. Inter-observer variability is the largest source
  of error.
- Always take duplicate measurements and report the mean.
- Record whether sunglasses or a viewscope were used; these
  systematically affect readings and must be consistent within a
  dataset.
- For Secchi tubes, verify the graduation markings against a ruler at
  least once per year.
- When both a Secchi disk and a turbidity meter are available, pair
  the measurements to develop a site-specific Secchi-turbidity
  regression for future use.


## 9. References

- Wetzel, R.G. and Likens, G.E. (2000). *Limnological Analyses*.

## 11. Training Record

Before performing Secchi measurements independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Perform supervised duplicate Secchi disk or Secchi tube measurements
   at one site
3. Demonstrate agreement within the QC criteria (0.5 m for disk, 2 cm
   for tube)
4. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
